current.caps: one round of 110 steps / 110 min for the outline and for each hole, then one fix round of 20 / 20; up to 2 tries per task
current.summary:
Scaffold v7, from what trial 5 and the outline probes taught. The outline task now starts with a plan: the method the leaf’s statement or paper names, and its steps, each a lemma in words. The outline then leaves every step as a `sorry` hole, combined by a short final proof; an outline has at most 12 holes and 300 lines. An outline that does not compile is not lost: the parts Lean rejects become holes (at most three passes), and an inline proof that is too long comes back as advice instead of a refusal.

As in v6, an outline whose hole is the leaf’s main claim is refused, every hole is first checked for a counterexample, and our index of prove2me’s library (333,690 statements) means the agent never re-proves what is already proved there and may import proved theorems.

The leaves: calibration leaf C07, and open leaves N03 and N05, chosen by quick outline probes. Since 15 November the node runs Qwen with multi-token prediction (MTP), which wrote long steps 1.7 to 1.9 times faster in our test on an RTX 3090.

trials.caps: 90 steps / 90 min for the outline and for each hole, then 2 fix rounds of 20 / 20; up to 2 tries per task
trials.summary: The model first writes an outline of the proof in which every step it has not proved is a sorry hole. Each hole then becomes a task of its own, after a quick pass of standard tactics, a ledger keeps every hole Lean has checked, and an assembly puts the pieces together. 2 of 3 leaves proved. F01, an open leaf that trials 3 and 4 had failed, was proved and accepted by prove2me: its first outline left the main claim in two holes, which failed twice; a second outline split the index into four fields, as the leaf’s own statement does, and all 6 of its holes were proved and assembled on the first try. Calibration leaf C12 was proved on the second try of its assembly. We stopped O02, which is not scored.
